ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that lines $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at point $O$. $OE$ and $OF$ are rays, $\angle AOE = 90^\circ$, and $OF$ bisects $\angle BOC$. If $\angle EOF = 30^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the construction, we have\\
$\because \angle AOE= 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle EOB= 180^\circ-\angle AOE= 90^\circ$.\\
$\because \angle EOF= 30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle FOB=\angle EOB-\angle EOF= 60^\circ$.\\
$\because$ OF bisects $\angle BOC$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOC=2\angle FOB= 120^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOD=180^\circ-\angle BOC=\boxed{60^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached diagram, AB is a horizontal straight line through O, with A on the left and B on the right, so OA and OB are opposite rays. CD is another straight line through O, with C in the upper-left direction and D in the lower-right direction, so OC and OD are opposite rays. Ray OE goes vertically upward from O, and ray OF goes upward-right from O between OE and OB. Reasoning: From the text, ∠AOE = 90°. Since OA and OB are opposite rays on the straight line AB, ∠AOB = 180°, so ∠EOB = 180° − ∠AOE = 180° − 90° = 90°. The image shows OF lies between OE and OB, and the text gives ∠EOF = 30°, so ∠FOB = ∠EOB − ∠EOF = 90° − 30° = 60°. Since OF bisects ∠BOC, ∠BOC = 2 × ∠FOB = 2 × 60° = 120°. Since C, O, D are collinear, ∠BOC and ∠BOD form a linear pair, so ∠BOD = 180° − 120° = 60°.
